Emma: heads-up — after the kernel rewrite we saw a P95 tail increase on m60 for chat routes. Quick profiling shows the prefix cache hit rate dropped from ~72% -> ~49% across a 24h window.
Raj: do we have a breakdown by prompt type (system vs user vs tool-heavy)?
Emma: yes — the biggest delta is system prompts that include function-call / tool metadata. Hypothesis: tokenizer token-id remapping changed the tokenizer hash we put in the cache key, and batching changes altered token boundaries. So reads no longer match previous keys.
Liam: a tokenizer remap would absolutely invalidate keys if we include tokenizer-derived ids. Do we currently include tokenizer version in the key?
Emma: current key schema is: `model|route|prompt_signature|tokenizer_hash|tool_args_json_sorted`. tokenizer_hash comes from tokenizer.vocab._version which we stopped pinning when we rolled the runtime patch.
Sophia: options: pin tokenizer version in key (stable but may require backfill) OR make key canonicalization ignore ephemeral differences (whitespace, quote styles, tool argument ordering). Both have trade-offs.
Dmitri: also saw warmup/backfill hasn't replayed system prompts with tool args — our backfill job focuses on user-only flows. That explains some of the warmup hit drop.
Raj: fallback reads are possible but expensive. Could we implement a tolerant read path that tries normalized key variants with limited probes? E.g., probe legacy tokenizer hash then a canonicalized prompt key. 
Emma: agreed. Proposal for a short experiment:
 1) Read path: try exact key, then if miss try legacy-tokenizer-hash fallback (count metric), then try normalized-tool-args key (opt-in). Limit to 2 fallback probes.
 2) Write path: include explicit `tokenizer_version` and add `stable_prompt_fingerprint` which is the normalized prompt string (unicode-normalized, strip zero-width, canonicalize JSON args with sorted keys and stable separators).
Liam: that would reduce false negatives. Also suggest making tool-arg keys TTL-shorter (e.g., 1d) since tool ordering churns more.
Sophia: I'll own A/B to validate normalization: 10% traffic runs with `ignore_tool_order` canonicalization, log fallback hits and per-route latency.
Emma: here's a tiny normalizer snippet we can use as reference:
```python
def normalize_prompt(p):
    p = unicode_normalize(p)
    p = strip_zero_width(p)
    if looks_like_json_args(p):
        args = parse_json(p)
        args = sort_keys_recursively(args)
        return json.dumps(args, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)
    return p
```
Dmitri: I'll add a targeted warmup backfill job that replays system+tool flows to the prefix cache for the next 48h. That should recover some hit rate quickly.
perf-bot: 24h baseline (pre-bump): hit_rate=72.1%, avg_latency=68ms, p95=120ms. Post-bump: hit_rate=49.3%, avg_latency=82ms, p95=200ms.
Raj: good data. Action items:
- eng-runtime: implement read-fallback probes + metrics for fallback_hit_ratio (Emma)
- infra: run targeted warmup backfill for system+tool flows (Dmitri)
- perf/devex: crew to own A/B experiment for `ignore_tool_order` canonicalization and dashboard widgets (Sophia)
Emma: I'll open a short RFC and a canary PR today. Will add dashboard widgets: hit_rate by route, fallback_ratio, warmup_backfill_progress.
Sophia: thanks — aim to start canary tomorrow and check fallback_ratio within the first 2h. :thumbsup:
